text:
james_support: @nina fyi — customer 'acme-fin' on Dedicated eu-west reports failing tool calls after we renamed the tool. They see a 400 schema validation error sometimes and 404s other times. trace=tr-9f8a. Sample request/resp below, happening from both our SDK and raw curl. Urgent; customer is blocked.

james_support: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/call 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"toolName":"pdf_extractor","args":{"url":"https://..."}}'

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"schema_validation_failed","details":["unknown tool 'pdf_extractor'"]}
```

nina_engineer: Thanks. Can you paste the request-id from the gateway logs and whether this is on Private/Dedicated control plane? Also which SDK version and platform?

james_support: Request-id gw:1758212345-rcp. Dedicated (eu-west-1) — customer using our SDK v2.3.1 but they also repro with raw curl from their infra. Happening intermittently since ~1758209000; started after they confirmed they renamed on their side last night.

ops-bot: registry-sync EVENT: rename applied: old_name=pdf_extractor -> new_name=pdf.extractor at 1758209500; alias-backfill started; edge-cache-ttl=3600s. Target routing entries updated in control plane but some edge caches still showing old entries.

kevin_sre: Hypothesis: router/edge cache still has mixed entries (old underscore name vs new dotted name), and our alias resolver is case-sensitive for the tool key. Two things to try fast: 1) flush router alias cache for that customer pool, 2) ask customer to call using the tool UUID or the old alias as a temporary workaround. Quick flush example (run on control-plane):

```
# invalidate per-customer alias cache
POST /internal/admin/v1/cache/invalidate
{ "scope": "customer:acme-fin", "keys": ["tool_aliases"] }
```

or run: `kubectl -n redwood-router rollout restart deployment/router-eu-west` (short blip). Doing one of these should stop the 404s within TTL.

nina_engineer: Also seeing a few router logs where incoming toolName header is mixed-case: `Pdf.Extractor` vs `pdf.extractor` vs `pdf_extractor`. Our lookup path lowercases and dot-normalizes in some codepaths but not others — that mismatch explains the intermittent schema vs unknown-tool errors. We'll patch to casefold + normalize underscores/dots in the resolver.

sara_support: Customer note: "We only renamed to pdf.extractor, we didn't change case. Some of our services are older and still emit pdf_extractor. We tried the old alias and it worked for a minute, then failed again." :disappointed:

kevin_sre: That matches cache propagation + duplicate keyspace (underscore vs dot). Plan: 1) immediate: invalidate alias cache for acme-fin and advise customer to use old alias as temp or call by tool_uuid; 2) next-release hotfix: alias resolver tolerant to case + underscore/dot variations and backfill alias index (write migration to insert alternative keys). I'll own rollout and will coordinate a rolling restart window. ETA for hotfix and backfill ~2h.

nina_engineer: I'll open a small changelist to normalize incoming tool identifiers and add a fallback resolver that checks an alternative-key map. Will include unit tests. Patch will include a short migration: for each alias X insert X.lower(), X.replace('_','.'), X.replace('.','_') into alias_index (only if missing).

james_support: Great — I'll relay workaround + ETA to customer. Workaround: call with tool_uuid or temporarily use the old alias; we will invalidate caches now. Thanks team :thumbsup:

sara_support: Customer updated: they can confirm 1) using tool_uuid works, 2) after the cache invalidate they saw fewer 404s but still hit a couple of 400s when services sent mixed-case. We'll expect the hotfix. Keep me posted.

nina_engineer: Will post the PR and deployment window here when ready.```
